title: Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel and the Nawab of Junagadh: The Will of the People Over Royal Whim (1947)
summary: In autumn 1947, Deputy Prime Minister Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel brilliantly outmaneuvered the autocratic Nawab of Junagadh, establishing that democratic accession belongs to the people, not royal dictators.
keywords: Historical Dialogue 175: நேருவும் விமர்சனமும்: “சிலர் என்னால் சோர்ந்திருக்கலாம்”
full_text:
In August 1947, as independent India worked to integrate over five hundred princely states into a coherent union, a dangerous constitutional crisis erupted in the Kathiawar peninsula of Gujarat.

The princely state of Junagadh was surrounded entirely by Indian territory, and over eighty percent of its population favored joining the Indian Union. However, its eccentric Nawab, Mahabat Khan, unilaterally declared accession to Pakistan.

Deputy Prime Minister Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel acted with characteristic iron resolve. When the Nawab’s dewan sought to justify the arbitrary decision, Patel responded with uncompromising democratic clarity:
"A princely state is not the private hunting estate of an autocrat. Sovereignty does not reside in the whim of a ruler; it belongs to the people who inhabit the soil! Junagadh is organically intertwined with India geographically, economically, and culturally. No arbitrary signature can sever a people from their homeland!"

As the local population rebelled against the ruler's autocratic decree, the Nawab fled by private plane to Karachi.

Refusing to rely merely on military intervention, Patel insisted upon the gold standard of democratic legitimacy: a free plebiscite. In February 1948, the citizens of Junagadh voted overwhelmingly—over 99 percent—to confirm their accession to the Republic of India. Patel proved that democratic popular will is the supreme arbiter of nationhood.
